name: Closed Stretches on the Highway
description:
Amazon's delivery vans use one long highway with kilometre markers 0, 1, 2, ... The highway authority has announced n road closures. Closure i blocks the road from marker l to marker r, which is (r - l) kilometres long. Closures can overlap, sit inside each other, or just touch (a closure ending at marker 12 and another starting at marker 12 form one continuous closed stretch).

The routing team needs two numbers: the total number of kilometres that are closed (each kilometre counted once, even if several closures cover it), and the number of separate continuous closed stretches.

Input: The first line has an integer n. Each of the next n lines has two integers l and r.
Output: Two integers separated by a space: total closed kilometres, then the number of separate stretches.

Constraints:
- 1 <= n <= 100000
- 0 <= l < r <= 1000000000
- Closures are given in no particular order

Amazon OA pattern: sort + merge intervals (Merge Intervals was reported 12 times in Amazon OAs, Oct 2026).

solution.code:
import sys
from collections import deque
import heapq
def s_ob2q1(n, segs):
    segs = sorted(segs); total = 0; cnt = 0
    cl, cr = segs[0]
    for l, r in segs[1:]:
        if l <= cr: cr = max(cr, r)
        else: total += cr - cl; cnt += 1; cl, cr = l, r
    total += cr - cl; cnt += 1
    return f"{total} {cnt}"

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
if data:
    n = data[0]
    print(s_ob2q1(n, [(data[1 + 2 * i], data[2 + 2 * i]) for i in range(n)]))

test_cases.description: (2,5) and (4,8) overlap into 2..8 (6 km); (10,12) and (12,13) touch at km 12 so they join into 10..13 (3 km). Total 9 km in 2 stretches.
The first closure covers the other two completely, so only one stretch of 100 km is closed.

name: Most Valuable Same-Day Orders
description:
A small Amazon packing station has n orders waiting. Packing any order takes exactly one hour, and the station packs one order at a time, in hours 1, 2, 3, and so on. Order i has a deadline d (it only counts if it is packed in an hour h with h <= d) and a value v. The station may skip orders.

Choose which orders to pack, and in which hours, so that the total value of orders packed on time is as large as possible. Print that total.

Input: The first line has an integer n. Each of the next n lines has two integers d and v.
Output: A single integer, the largest possible total value.

Constraints:
- 1 <= n <= 100000
- 1 <= d <= 1000000000
- 1 <= v <= 1000000000
- The answer can exceed the 32-bit integer range

Amazon OA pattern: sort + greedy with a heap (sorting + greedy is the most reported Amazon OA topic, Aug-Nov 2026).

test_cases.description: Best plan: 50 and 40 (deadline 2) in hours 1 and 2, then 20 (deadline 3) in hour 3, total 110. Packing 30 (deadline 1) in hour 1 would push out the 40 and give only 100.
Every order must finish in hour 1, so only one can be packed: the most valuable, 9.
